evidence.excerpt: Polyetherimide (PEI) is used in precision-fit diagnostic device components where dimensional tolerances of ±0.02 mm or tighter are required. This work tracks dimensional changes in injection-moulded PEI discs and pins stored in sealed packaging at three relative humidity levels (30%, 60%, and 90%) over 18 months. CMM measurements at six-month intervals show that at 90% RH, average diameter growth reached 0.015 mm after 18 months, representing 75% of the maximum allowable tolerance. Moisture uptake at 90% RH reached 1.2 wt%, consistent with literature values for unfilled PEI. Specimens stored at 30% RH showed negligible dimensional change (<0.003 mm). A linear predictive model relating absorbed moisture to dimensional deviation, validated against independent specimens, is presented with 95% confidence intervals. The study provides evidence to support the use of desiccant packaging with a humidity indicator below 40% RH for long shelf-life storage of PEI diagnostic components.
